facts.explanation: Speed records span an enormous range: a spacecraft diving toward the Sun moves faster than anything built for people. Among crewed craft, the Apollo astronauts returning from the Moon still hold the record, while records on land, rail and water sit far lower.

facts.query: When did people first fly, reach the poles, climb Everest and walk on the Moon?
facts.topic: Great firsts of exploration and speed
facts.explanation: Within a single lifetime, people went from the first powered aeroplane hop to walking on the Moon. Along the way they reached the South Pole, crossed the Atlantic alone by air, broke the sound barrier, climbed Everest, broke the famous barrier in the mile and touched the deepest point of the ocean.

facts.description: Orville Wright makes the first controlled, powered aeroplane flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

facts.query: How long are the waves used by radio, Wi-Fi, GPS and Blu-ray?
facts.explanation: Radio, Wi-Fi, phone networks and disc players all use electromagnetic waves, differing mainly in wavelength.
